name: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN)
note: The Guyana Revenue Authority's Tax Operations Policy No. 8 – Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) (26 July 2019), as archive.org's snapshot of 20 September 2025 holds it (the GRA's live site answered 403 to this research), read 2026-10-31: the TIN is a unique computer-generated number allocated to each taxpayer, individual or business; the GRA is the only agency authorised to issue it; under s. 2 of the Income Tax Amendment (No. 2) Act 2006 every person conducting business with a government department, public authority (the GRA included), public corporation or the Bank of Guyana must have one; persons under fifteen, temporary residents not in receipt of income (stays of no more than 183 days) and persons with no income are exempt, except when transacting business with the GRA; an individual applies with the application form, an identity paper and proof of address. The length is the GRA's own, in its notice 'Change to Partnership TIN' (3 November 2022), as archive.org's snapshot of 20 September 2025 holds it (the site files the notice under an unrelated address, the snapshot's): partnerships issued a TIN before the Optimal Revenue Management System use the numeral 2 instead of 0 as the first digit of 'their nine-digit TIN', the other eight digits unchanged. The Government Information Agency, as Stabroek News reported it on 26 January 2008, read 2026-10-31, described the TIN as 'a unique computer-generated nine-digit number'. READINGS: the nine digits are read as every TIN's length, the 2022 notice stating it of partnerships' TINs and the 2008 statement of the TIN in general; no structure beyond partnerships' first digit (2) is given, so the pattern holds any nine digits; 'who' is read as anyone, the policy allocating a TIN to each taxpayer and requiring it of every person dealing with the bodies named, citizen or not; 'when' is on application. The GRA's leaflet's G$1,000 is for the TIN certificate and isn't held as the number's fee. No check digit, age or time is stated.

sources.title: Guyana Revenue Authority, Tax Operations Policy No. 8 – Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) (26 July 2019; archive.org snapshot of 20 September 2025)
sources.said: A Taxpayer Identification Number, commonly known as TIN , is a unique computer generated number allocated to each taxpayer, whether they are an individual, a Commercial Business, a Government Department, Public Corporation, or a Special Body. The GRA is the only agency authorised to issue a TIN. ... every person conducting business with a Government Department, Public Authority (including GRA), Public Corporation or the Central Bank (Bank of Guyana) is required to have a TIN. ... Any person under the age of fifteen years old (15 years).

sources.title: Guyana Revenue Authority, Change to Partnership TIN (3 November 2022; archive.org snapshot of 20 September 2025)
sources.said: Change to Partnership TIN November 3, 2022 ... are required to use the numeral ‘2’ instead of zero (0) as the first digit in their nine-digit TIN when signing up/ registering for Optimal e-services . The other eight digits will remain the same.

sources.title: Stabroek News, '80 taxpayers issued TIN – GRA' (26 January 2008)
sources.said: GINA said TIN is a unique computer-generated nine-digit number which identifies persons for the purpose of transacting business with the GRA and other agencies specified under the law.
